title: Deterministic slew-credit ledger with request prioritization for Dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a deterministic per-tenant 'slew-credit ledger' that governs temporary burst capacity, enforces safety limits, and interacts with the autoscaling policy engine to prioritize and degrade requests predictably during congestion.

Background: Dedicated fleets need a way to provide throughput guarantees while allowing measured bursts without violating global fleet safety limits or surprising customers. Current autoscalers react to aggregate signals and do not encode deterministic, auditable per-tenant burst budgets or request-class prioritization. This causes noisy scaling and occasional SLA thrashing during correlated load spikes.

High-level design:
- Maintain a per-tenant ledger of 'slew credits' (integer tokens) that are consumed by requests that exceed reserved throughput. Credits are replenished deterministically on a replenishment schedule derived from committed capacity and negotiated burst allowances.
- Implement request classes (priority tiers): control-plane (high), interactive (normal), background (low). Each class has separate debit rules and configurable preemption weights.
- Deterministic accounting: use single-threaded ledger transaction batches per routing shard to avoid races; all updates are idempotent and append-only for auditability.
- Autoscaler integration: ledger headroom is exposed as a target metric to the policy engine. When aggregated ledger utilization crosses thresholds, the autoscaler triggers bounded ramp increases or fallbacks to cheaper model variants.
- Safety limits: global hard caps, per-tenant max burst, minimum sustained-reserve floor, and a decay curve for credit recovery to avoid credit bank runs.

Why deterministic ledger: avoids transient over-scaling, gives predictable client-facing behavior (documentable burst windows), and enables clear cost accounting and rollback during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Ledger records per-tenant credit consumption and replenishment with <=10ms write latency under peak routing shard load
Request scoring honors priority tiers and enforces preemption rules: high interrupts low when no credits available
Autoscaler reads aggregated ledger metrics and performs bounded ramp-up without violating global hard-cap in >1000 synthetic spike tests
Audit log contains immutable transaction IDs linking requests -> ledger debits -> autoscaler decisions for at least 7 days
Can toggle ledger enforcement via runtime feature flag per environment and rollback within one minute
design_notes: Credit model: two components: 'committed' (reservoir tied to reserved capacity) and 'bonus' (time-limited burst allowance). Bonus decays exponentially or via a configurable linear window depending on tenant SLA.

Transaction model: ledger shard receives a deterministic batch sequence number; routing nodes submit batch intents and get either 'commit' or 'reject' atomically. This prevents double-spend across concurrent routing nodes.

Scaling algorithm coupling: use a hysteresis-aware bounded-linear ramp: when aggregate ledger depletion > 70% for 60s, request a +10%-25% fleet increment with a cool-down proportional to previous ramps. Avoids immediate large commits that waste cost.

Safety fences: global hard-cap enforced in both routing and orchestra layers. Even if autoscaler requests capacity, the allocator will not exceed the hard cap. Fallbacks include reducing model size, restricting background classes, or returning 429 with enriched Retry-After when policy permits.

Edge cases: sudden tenant churn, clock skew between shards, and cross-shard debit collisions. Mitigations include lease-based replenishment, monotonic counters, and conservative defaults for new tenants.
rollout_plan: Phase A: feature-flagged internal-only with 3 tenants (canary) for 2 weeks; monitor ledger consistency, latency, and autoscaler interactions. Phase B: open to all internal Dedicated fleets with opt-in for tenants that have committed throughput. Phase C: enable for new tenants by default and expose controls in Console (burst allowance sliders and priority mappings). Rollback via feature-flag and emergency kill-switch in Control Plane (route-level enforcement).
engineering_updates: 2026-03-11: Prototype of ledger transaction model implemented in routing shard (branch: feat/ledger-proto). Added unit tests for single-node debits.
2026-03-12: Performance regression found in naive write path under fanout; switched to batched append with in-memory coalescing. P95 write latency improved from 28ms -> 9ms.
2026-03-13: Integrated simple priority preemption in router; observed deterministic preemption in local integration tests. Working on cross-shard batch ordering.

2026-03-14: First end-to-end with autoscaler metrics exposed (dashboard created). Observed autoscaler ramp requests triggered appropriately in synthetic spike. Open PR: github.com/redwood-inference/alloc/PR-1123
Next: implement audit-log immutability plumbing and Circuit Breaker for global hard-cap enforcement. Schedule design review with SRE and Security next week.
review_feedback: PM (Rohit Sengupta): prefer exposing burst allowance as both absolute tokens and % of committed throughput for easier tenant configuration.
SRE (Lena Morris): require explicit backpressure path documented for the Console runbook; avoid subtle 429 spikes that cascade across upstreams.
Security (Jinsoo Park): audit log must be WORM for at least 7 days and include tenant identity hashed with non-reversible salt; asked to include KMS key usage in implementation plan.
Design (Maya Nguyen): suggest a UI mock for priority mapping and clearer defaults for 'interactive' vs 'background' classes.
